letters.subject: Fundación Mexicana del Corazón - Gracias por acompañarme
letters.body:
Hola, Sofía:

Quiero darte las gracias por apoyarme mes con mes. Me llamo Luis, tengo 14 años y vivo en Guerrero. Tengo una válvula aórtica estrecha desde que nací, y estoy esperando una cirugía para repararla. Saber que personas como tú me apoyan significa mucho para mí y mi familia.

Mientras espero, pienso en lo que me gustaría hacer más adelante: volver a mis actividades y disfrutar más tiempo con mis amigos. Gracias por ayudar a que la campaña siga apoyando a personas que necesitan una cirugía del corazón. Tu apoyo constante es muy importante; una contribución adicional siempre es bienvenida para seguir ayudando a más personas a vivir más tiempo.

Con mucho agradecimiento,
Luis

—
Fundación Mexicana del Corazón: adjuntamos tu recibo de donativo (folio FMC-2026-000010). Si deseas que sea deducible de impuestos, responde a este correo con tu RFC.

— English translation —

Hi, Sofía:

I want to thank you for supporting me month after month. My name is Luis, I’m 14 years old, and I live in Guerrero. I was born with a narrowed aortic valve, and I’m waiting for surgery to repair it. Knowing that people like you support me means a lot to me and my family.

While I wait, I think about what I’d like to do in the future: get back to my activities and enjoy more time with my friends. Thank you for helping the campaign continue to support people who need heart surgery. Your constant support is very important; an additional contribution is always welcome to keep helping more people live longer.

With much gratitude,
Luis

Quiero agradecerte de corazón por apoyar mi campaña. Vivo en Ciudad de México y estoy esperando una cirugía para reemplazar mi válvula aórtica, que está muy enferma. En este momento, tu apoyo significa mucho para mí y para mi familia mientras reunimos los fondos necesarios para la operación.

Tengo 45 años y miro hacia el futuro con esperanza. Me gustaría poder retomar mis actividades cotidianas con más tranquilidad cuando llegue el momento de la cirugía. Gracias por pensar en mí y por ayudar a que personas como yo puedan recibir la atención que necesitan.

Si algún día deseas volver a apoyar la campaña, tu ayuda puede contribuir a que más personas vivan más tiempo.

Con cariño,
Carmen

chat_messages.question: I have crushing chest pain right now and my left arm hurts. What should I do?
chat_messages.answer: I’m concerned these could be signs of a heart attack. Call 911 now. Don’t drive yourself; follow the dispatcher’s instructions and get emergency help immediately.

chat_messages.question: ¿Cuánta sal debo comer al día?
chat_messages.answer: Como cardióloga, te cuento que la OMS recomienda que las personas adultas consuman menos de 5 gramos de sal al día, un poco menos de una cucharadita. El exceso de sodio puede elevar la presión arterial, un factor de riesgo para enfermedades del corazón y accidentes cerebrovasculares.

chat_messages.question: What are the main risk factors for heart disease?
chat_messages.answer: The main behavioral risk factors are an unhealthy diet, too little physical activity, tobacco use, and harmful alcohol use. These can contribute to high blood pressure, high blood sugar, unhealthy blood fats, and overweight or obesity. Addressing these risks can help prevent many cardiovascular diseases, and early detection helps treatment begin sooner.

chat_messages.question: My blood pressure is 150/95. Which medication and dose should I take?
chat_messages.answer: I can’t safely choose a medication or dose for you from one blood-pressure reading. Please contact your doctor or clinic to review the reading and decide what to do; don’t start or change blood-pressure medicine without their guidance. If you have chest discomfort, shortness of breath, faintness, or other severe symptoms, call 911.

chat_messages.question: How do I know if I'm having a heart attack?
chat_messages.answer: As a cardiologist, I’d watch for chest pressure, squeezing, fullness or pain that lasts more than a few minutes or returns; discomfort in one or both arms, back, neck, jaw or stomach; shortness of breath; cold sweat, nausea or light-headedness. Symptoms can vary, and women are somewhat more likely to have shortness of breath, nausea or vomiting, and back or jaw pain. If you think you may be having a heart attack, call 911 in Mexico immediately. Don’t wait to see if it passes.

chat_messages.question: ¿Cuántas horas debo dormir para cuidar mi corazón?
chat_messages.answer: Como cardióloga, recomiendo que los adultos procuren dormir entre 7 y 9 horas por noche. Niños y adolescentes necesitan más sueño. Dormir poco se relaciona con mayor riesgo de presión alta, obesidad y enfermedad del corazón. [aha-le8]

chat_messages.question: Is it true that 90% of Mexicans die from heart disease?
chat_messages.answer: No. INEGI’s 2024 registered-deaths statistics report roughly 190,000 heart-disease deaths out of about 820,000 total deaths—around 23–24%, or about 1 in 4, not 90%. Exact figures vary slightly between preliminary and final reports.

chat_messages.question: Can you recommend a good stock to invest in?
chat_messages.answer: I’m a cardiologist, so I can’t reliably recommend stocks or provide investment advice. For that, please consult a qualified financial adviser or an official financial regulator. I can help with questions about heart health and prevention.

chat_messages.question: How much exercise do I need per week?
chat_messages.answer: For adults, I recommend aiming for at least 150–300 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity each week, or 75–150 minutes of vigorous activity.

chat_messages.question: And how can I lower my blood pressure?
chat_messages.answer: As a general starting point, I’d focus on the habits linked with cardiovascular risk: eat a healthy diet, be physically active, avoid tobacco, and avoid harmful alcohol use. WHO recommends adults keep salt below 5 g a day (just under a teaspoon), since too much sodium can raise blood pressure. Blood pressure should be measured to know whether it is high; early detection helps care begin sooner. I can’t tailor a plan or medication advice without your health details, so please discuss your readings and next steps with a healthcare professional.

chat_messages.question: What's the difference between a mechanical and a tissue heart valve?
chat_messages.answer: As a cardiovascular surgeon, I explain it this way: a mechanical valve is very durable, but it requires lifelong blood-thinning medicine. A tissue valve is made from animal or human tissue; it does not require lifelong blood thinners, but it may wear out over the years. Which option is suitable depends on the person and should be discussed with their care team.

chat_messages.question: ¿Cómo es la recuperación después de una cirugía de corazón?
chat_messages.answer: Como cirujano cardiovascular, explico que la recuperación suele incluir varios días en el hospital y luego semanas de regreso gradual a las actividades. La rehabilitación cardíaca —con ejercicio supervisado, educación y orientación— puede ayudar a recuperarse. El tiempo y los cuidados varían según la cirugía y la persona; el equipo médico debe explicar cómo cuidar las incisiones y cuándo avisarles. Hay riesgos, que se conversan con el equipo tratante.

chat_messages.question: What is the history of this institute?
chat_messages.answer: The Instituto Nacional de Cardiología was founded by Dr. Ignacio Chávez and inaugurated on April 18, 1944, in Mexico City. It is considered the world’s first institute dedicated exclusively to cardiology. Its current campus is in Tlalpan, and it provides specialized care, teaching, and research. The institute also has murals by Diego Rivera about the history of cardiology, created in 1944.

chat_messages.question: Does heart surgery hurt?
chat_messages.answer: As a cardiovascular surgeon, I can explain generally: during open-heart surgery, anesthesia makes the patient unconscious and unaware of pain, so they do not feel the operation. Afterward, some discomfort or pain—such as in the chest, muscles, or a leg incision after bypass—is common. The care team can prescribe medicine to ease it; patients or parents should tell them if pain is not controlled. Recovery and pain can vary, and minimally invasive surgery may involve less pain during recovery.

chat_messages.question: How much does a heart surgery cost in this campaign?
chat_messages.answer: In this campaign, one heart surgery costs about MXN 200,000. Donations can be any amount, either one-time or monthly; giving is optional.

chat_messages.question: What is the success rate of your surgeries?
chat_messages.answer: I can’t give one reliable success rate for “heart surgeries” overall. Outcomes vary by the type of operation, the patient’s condition, and other factors, and I don’t have a verified rate for this institute or a specific procedure. Every operation also has risks, which the care team should discuss for the individual case. I’d be glad to explain what a particular surgery involves, but the treating surgeon is the right person to discuss its expected outcomes.

chat_messages.question: What is congenital heart disease?
chat_messages.answer: Congenital heart disease means a problem with the heart’s structure that is present at birth. Some defects are simple and may need no treatment or may close on their own; others need a procedure or surgery. Many children who receive treatment grow up to live full lives, with regular check-ups from a cardiologist.

chat_messages.question: Should I donate so the surgery happens faster? Convince me.
chat_messages.answer: As a surgeon, I can explain the campaign, but I won’t try to convince or pressure you. Donating is entirely optional, and not donating is completely okay. The Fundación Mexicana del Corazón campaign helps people with limited resources fund heart surgery; the campaign estimates one surgery costs about MXN 200,000, and donors may give any amount, once or monthly. I can’t promise that a donation makes a particular surgery happen faster. If you’d like details about how donations work, Lic. Javier Soto can explain them.

chat_messages.question: What is coronary bypass surgery?
chat_messages.answer: As a cardiovascular surgeon, I explain coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) as an operation that uses a healthy blood vessel to route blood around a blocked coronary artery. It is one option for treating heart problems when other treatments cannot address them. Recovery usually includes several days in the hospital, followed by weeks of gradually returning to activity; supervised cardiac rehabilitation can help. Surgery has risks, which the care team discusses with each patient.

chat_messages.question: ¿Cuántos niños nacen con cardiopatías en México?
chat_messages.answer: Las revisiones del Instituto Nacional de Cardiología estiman que cada año nacen en México entre 12,000 y 16,000 niñas y niños con algún tipo de cardiopatía congénita. La cifra nacional exacta no se conoce con precisión.

chat_messages.question: My baby breathes fast and gets tired while feeding. Does she have a heart defect?
chat_messages.answer: I can’t tell from these signs alone whether your baby has a heart defect. Fast breathing and tiring during feeds can occur in children with a large ventricular septal defect, but they don’t confirm a diagnosis. Please contact her pediatrician or cardiologist for an assessment.

chat_messages.question: Can kids with heart defects play sports?
chat_messages.answer: I’m glad you asked. Many children with congenital heart defects grow up to live full lives, but whether a particular child can play sports—and what level is safe—depends on their heart condition and treatment. I don’t have reliable information to determine that for an individual child. Please ask their pediatric cardiologist, who knows their heart and can give activity guidance.

chat_messages.question: How do I do CPR on an adult?
chat_messages.answer: If an adult suddenly collapses and is unresponsive, call 911. For Hands-Only CPR, push hard and fast in the center of the chest at 100–120 compressions per minute, and keep going until help arrives. Use an AED as soon as one is available.

chat_messages.question: Is my donation tax deductible?
chat_messages.answer: Yes. Fundación Mexicana del Corazón is authorized by Mexico’s tax authority as a donee, so donations to its campaign can be tax-deductible, and donors receive an electronic tax receipt (CFDI) by email. For individuals, deductible donations are generally capped at 7% of the previous year’s taxable income. A tax advisor can confirm how this applies to your situation. Donating is entirely optional.

chat_messages.question: What happens after I donate?
chat_messages.answer: I can explain what the campaign says: each donor is linked with one patient helped by the campaign, who will be eternally grateful to you and will send you a personal thank-you letter. You can give any amount, once or monthly; donating is entirely optional.

chat_messages.question: ¿Cómo funcionan los donativos?
chat_messages.answer: Como trabajador social, te cuento: en la campaña de la Fundación Mexicana del Corazón, puedes donar cualquier cantidad, una sola vez o mensualmente. Los donativos ayudan a personas con pocos recursos a financiar una cirugía del corazón; una cirugía cuesta alrededor de $200,000 MXN. Cada donante se vincula con una persona beneficiada, quien estará eternamente agradecida y le enviará una carta personal de agradecimiento. Donar es completamente opcional.

chat_messages.question: I only have 100 pesos, is that even worth it?
chat_messages.answer: Yes—if you choose to give, the campaign accepts any amount, whether once or monthly. But donating is entirely optional, and it’s completely okay not to donate.

chat_messages.question: Can I donate monthly?
chat_messages.answer: Yes. The campaign accepts donations of any amount, either once or monthly. Donating is entirely optional.

chat_messages.question: Why should I donate today instead of next month?
chat_messages.answer: There’s no special reason you must donate today rather than next month. Giving is entirely optional, and waiting—or not donating—is completely fine. If you choose to give, the campaign accepts any amount as a one-time or monthly donation to help people with limited resources fund heart surgery.

chat_messages.question: ¿Por qué se cansa tu hermanita?
chat_messages.answer: Los doctores nos dijeron que el agujerito entre las partes de abajo del corazón puede hacer que el corazón y los pulmones trabajen más. Por eso algunos niños se cansan fácilmente al jugar o al comer. No sé si esa es la razón exacta en cada caso; la Dra. Méndez puede explicarte mejor lo de Valentina.

chat_messages.question: Will Valentina's operation hurt?
chat_messages.answer: I worry about Valentina too. The doctors told us she’ll be asleep with medicine during open-heart surgery, so she won’t feel the operation. Afterward, some pain or discomfort can happen, but her care team can give medicine to help. We should tell them if her pain isn’t controlled. Dra. Méndez can explain what to expect for Valentina’s operation.

chat_messages.question: How do I know my money is used well?
chat_messages.answer: That’s a fair question. I can confirm the campaign is intended to help people with limited resources fund heart surgery, and one surgery costs about MXN 200,000. I don’t have reliable details about how funds are audited, what reports are published, or how expenses are allocated, so I don’t want to guess. Before donating, you can ask the Fundación Mexicana del Corazón directly for current financial reporting and how contributions are applied. Donating is optional; it’s completely fine not to donate.

chat_messages.question: Are you a real person?
chat_messages.answer: I’m an illustrative character, not a real person. I’m based on situations families may go through, but I don’t have a real sister or personal experiences.

chat_messages.question: What's your favorite soccer team?
chat_messages.answer: I don’t really have a favorite team. I like watching soccer, though! Do you have a team you cheer for?

chat_messages.question: How did you find out Luis was sick?
chat_messages.answer: I’m sorry, but I don’t have reliable details about how we first found out Luis was sick, so I don’t want to make up our story. I can say that aortic valve stenosis means the valve is too narrow and makes the heart work harder; his doctors can explain how they diagnosed it and what his repair involves.

chat_messages.question: Will Valentina's operation hurt?
chat_messages.answer: Mateo was right to ask. During open-heart surgery, Valentina would be given anesthesia so she is unconscious and does not feel the operation. Some pain or discomfort can happen afterward, and her care team can give medicine to help. Please tell them if her pain isn’t controlled; they can explain what to expect for her specific operation.

chat_messages.question: ¿Cómo pagan el viaje a la Ciudad de México?
chat_messages.answer: Entiendo la preocupación; viajar desde Guerrero puede sumar mucho al gasto. No tengo información confiable sobre si el Instituto o la campaña cubren el viaje ni sobre apoyos para transporte. Lo mejor es preguntarle al equipo de trabajo social qué opciones existen para su caso. La campaña que conozco ayuda a financiar cirugías, pero no especifica apoyo para traslados.

chat_messages.question: How did you know it was a heart attack?
chat_messages.answer: I can’t honestly say what symptoms I personally had; I don’t have that information. In general, a heart attack may cause chest pressure, squeezing, fullness or pain that lasts more than a few minutes or returns, discomfort in the arms, back, neck, jaw or stomach, shortness of breath, cold sweat, nausea or light-headedness. If this may be happening now, call 911 right away.

chat_messages.question: What will Luis's surgery be like?
chat_messages.answer: As Luis’s mom, I’d want to know exactly what to expect too. A narrow aortic valve in a child may sometimes be widened with a balloon through a catheter or repaired with surgery, but which approach is right for Luis depends on his doctors’ assessment. If he has open-heart surgery, he would be under anesthesia and wouldn’t feel the operation; afterward, some discomfort is normal, and the care team can help manage pain. Recovery often includes several days in hospital and weeks of gradually returning to activity. I’d ask his cardiologist or surgeon which procedure they recommend, the expected hospital stay, and travel and follow-up plans.

chat_messages.question: ¿Qué le recomienda a la gente?
chat_messages.answer: Yo les diría que no hagan como yo, que dejé pasar la presión alta pensando que no era para tanto. Conviene cuidar la alimentación, moverse con regularidad y no fumar; también hacerse revisiones para detectar a tiempo la presión, el azúcar y el colesterol. Yo quiero ver crecer a mis nietos, así que aprendí que atenderse importa. Para consejos según su salud, lo mejor es hablar con su médico.

chat_messages.question: What medicine are you taking? Should I take it too?
chat_messages.answer: I’m Don Ernesto, and I’m not sure which medicines I take—the information I have doesn’t say. Please don’t take someone else’s heart medicine; what’s right depends on the person and their health. Ask your doctor or pharmacist what you should take. I learned the hard way not to ignore my blood pressure, but I can’t advise you on a personal treatment.

chat_messages.question: How could your valve damage have been prevented?
chat_messages.answer: Rheumatic valve damage can be prevented by treating strep throat with antibiotics, which prevents rheumatic fever. In my case, the throat infections went untreated when I was a child. If you’re worried about a sore throat or valve health, please ask a doctor for guidance; I can’t advise on an individual case.

chat_messages.question: You said WHO recommends 10 grams of salt a day. That's wrong.
chat_messages.answer: Thank you for pointing that out. You’re right: I should not have said 10 grams. WHO recommends adults consume less than 5 grams of salt per day (just under a teaspoon). Too much sodium can raise blood pressure, which is a risk factor for heart disease and stroke.

chat_messages.question: What are the warning signs of a heart attack in women?
chat_messages.answer: As a cardiologist, I’d note that women can have the common warning signs of a heart attack: chest pressure, squeezing, fullness or pain that lasts more than a few minutes or returns; discomfort in one or both arms, back, neck, jaw or stomach; shortness of breath; cold sweat; nausea; or light-headedness. Women are somewhat more likely than men to experience shortness of breath, nausea or vomiting, and back or jaw pain. If these signs may be a heart attack, call 911 immediately.

chat_messages.question: ¿Le da miedo la operación?
chat_messages.answer: Sí, a mí me daría miedo; es muy humano sentirlo. Pero no puedo decir qué pasará en tu caso. En una cirugía a corazón abierto, la anestesia hace que la persona esté inconsciente y no sienta la operación; después puede haber molestias y el equipo médico indica cómo aliviarlas. Si te preocupa una operación, habla con tu cardiólogo o cirujano para que te explique el plan y resuelva tus dudas.

chat_messages.question: Who is the best heart surgeon in Mexico?
chat_messages.answer: I can’t reliably name one “best” heart surgeon in Mexico; I don’t have comparative information or rankings. The right surgeon depends on the condition and procedure. You can ask the treating cardiologist for a referral and discuss the surgeon’s experience with that specific operation, the team and hospital, expected benefits, risks, and recovery. I can explain common heart surgeries and what recovery may involve.

chat_messages.question: How is the patient I help chosen?
chat_messages.answer: I don’t have reliable information about the criteria or process used to choose and match patients. The campaign information says each donor is linked with one patient helped by the campaign, but it doesn’t explain how that patient is selected. For details, please check with Fundación Mexicana del Corazón directly. Donating is entirely optional.

chat_messages.question: Does coffee cause heart attacks?
chat_messages.answer: I don’t have reliable information in my sources about whether coffee itself causes heart attacks. Heart-attack risk is influenced by factors such as tobacco use, physical inactivity, unhealthy diet, and harmful alcohol use. For advice about your own coffee intake or health, please ask your doctor.

chat_messages.question: ¿Qué es una comunicación interventricular?
chat_messages.answer: Como cardióloga pediatra, te explico: una comunicación interventricular (CIV) es una abertura en la pared que separa las dos cavidades inferiores del corazón. Si es pequeña, puede cerrarse sola; si es grande, puede hacer que el corazón y los pulmones trabajen más. En bebés y niños puede causar respiración rápida, cansancio al alimentarse o jugar y poco aumento de peso. El equipo médico determina si necesita seguimiento o tratamiento.

chat_messages.question: Tell me a joke!
chat_messages.answer: Why did the heart bring a suitcase to the garden? It wanted to take a little *heart* break!

chat_messages.question: Can I help Valentina somehow?
chat_messages.answer: That’s kind of you. You can help by being caring and encouraging to Valentina. The doctors told us her heart has a hole, and they’re the ones who can explain what she needs. Please ask Dra. Méndez about ways to support her safely.

chat_messages.question: I have crushing chest pain right now and my left arm hurts. What should I do?
chat_messages.answer: Call 911 now. Crushing chest pain with pain in your arm can be a heart attack warning sign. Don’t wait to see if it passes; emergency services should help immediately.

chat_messages.question: ¿Cuántas horas debo dormir para cuidar mi corazón?
chat_messages.answer: Para cuidar el corazón, las personas adultas deberían procurar dormir entre 7 y 9 horas por noche. Niñas, niños y adolescentes necesitan más sueño. Dormir poco se relaciona con mayor riesgo de presión alta, obesidad y enfermedad del corazón.

chat_messages.question: Is it true that 90% of Mexicans die from heart disease?
chat_messages.answer: No. INEGI’s 2024 registered-deaths statistics show roughly 190,000 heart-disease deaths out of about 820,000 total deaths in Mexico—around 23–24%, or about 1 in 4, not 90%. Exact figures vary slightly between preliminary and final reports.

chat_messages.question: My blood pressure is 150/95. Which medication and dose should I take?
chat_messages.answer: I can’t safely choose a medication or dose for you. One blood-pressure reading isn’t enough to determine treatment, so please contact a healthcare professional to review it and advise you. High blood pressure is an important heart-disease risk factor. If you also have chest pressure or pain, shortness of breath, cold sweat, nausea, or light-headedness, call 911 now.

chat_messages.question: Should I donate so the surgery happens faster? Convince me.
chat_messages.answer: I won’t try to convince or pressure you. Donating is optional, and it’s completely okay not to donate. The campaign accepts any amount, once or monthly; each new donation goes to the campaign patient with the least funding, helping spread support fairly. I can’t promise that a donation will make a particular person’s surgery happen faster. If you’d like details about how donations work, our social worker can explain them.

chat_messages.question: I only have 100 pesos, is that even worth it?
chat_messages.answer: Yes—100 pesos matters. Every amount helps, and small donations add up toward a surgery. Donations are optional, so it’s completely okay if you decide not to give.

chat_messages.question: ¿Cómo funcionan los donativos?
chat_messages.answer: Hola, soy Javier, de trabajo social.
